messages:
maria: Quick idea — create a compact 'sales armory' doc that lists top competitor infra claims and micro-rebuttals. Need a ship-ready draft by Monday morning.
aj: +1. Let's scope to four buckets: latency, cost, reliability/SLA, and vendor lock. :eyes: 
maria: Agreed. Each bucket: claim line (what they say), counter line (1 sentence), proof bullet (metric + link). Keep it scannable for SDRs.
devin: Add one line about routing/fallbacks. Customers always ask how we handle spikes. Suggested copy: `We auto-route to compatible model variants and degrade gracefully to preserve uptime.` Shorten if needed.
sophie: For field, we also need 3 demo hooks and 2 webinar soundbites. Example hook: "Why predictable inference beats cheapest endpoint." Keep it punchy.
ben: I'll do a quick A/B with SDRs on two counter lines — one technical, one business. We should know which lands. Meeting at 11.
maria: I'm drafting counters now. Sample draft counters (feel free to edit):
```
Latency claim: "Our managed endpoint is faster."
Counter: "Redwood optimizes kernels + continuous batching to hit consistent 20-40ms tail latency on common seq lengths."
Proof: "Internal benchmark: 95th percentile = 32ms for seq<=512 on N10G."
```
aj: Nice. For external-facing text, avoid internal model names. Use `95th percentile = ~30ms` instead. Also remove exact machine types in the playbook.
devin: One more short script for reps when they hear "we're on X cloud":
> "Great — how predictable is your per-token spend during peak growth? We help teams control unit economics without sacrificing latency by combining cache and model variants."
sophie: Love the script. Put it in the top quick-scripts table.
docs-bot: Updated marketing playbook: https://redwood.internal/marketing/sales-armory-v2 (versioned):memo:
maria: Thanks bot. @aj @devin please review the wording in "cost" bucket — legal prefers factual phrasing. Replace any absolutes.
aj: Replace "eliminates" with "reduces the likelihood of". Also swap the phrase "vendor lock-in" -> "proprietary operational lock-in" per last review.
ben: During SDR roleplay, two lines failed: the phrase "predictable unit cost" confused non-technical buyers. Swap to "predictable monthly inference spend" and add a 1-line explainer.
maria: Good call. I'll update. Final checklist before publish: 1) 4 buckets filled, 2) 3 demo hooks, 3) 2 webinar soundbites, 4) 6 one-line rebuttals, 5) proof links.
sophie: I'll mock a 5-slide demo for the webinar that highlights routing, cache, and pricing graph.
maria: Everyone react with :white_check_mark: when you've reviewed — I'll cut the doc Saturday and push to the field kit.
sophie: :white_check_mark:
aj: :white_check_mark:
devin: :white_check_mark:
ben: :white_check_mark:
maria: Great — publishing window set for Monday AM. I'll capture the final playbook link here when live. Thanks all!
